shared.klass: Class: a mountain range for a square-grid strategy map, drawn as one raised terrain feature: one continuous ridge of connected rocky peaks that share a single rock mass, calmer and less saturated than units, thick single-colour black outline, simple shapes, no face and no eyes. It stands on the empty transparent background: nothing is drawn under it, no ground, no grass, no soil, no slab, no tile and no platform.
shared.negative: ground plate, platform, grass square, soil patch, slab, isometric block, background, buildings, characters, people, red, trees, forest, bushes, river, lake, boulders at the foot, separate rocks
shared.ridgeWide: Subject: a wide mountain range, twice as wide as it is tall: one continuous ridge of five or six steep cool grey stone peaks of different heights, joined by saddles into a single rock mass, small white snow caps on the highest peaks, big simple rock faces in two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; the ridge runs from the left edge of the image to the right edge; just rock and snow; the foot of the rock is the lowest thing in the image.
shared.ridgeSquare: Subject: a broad mountain massif as wide as it is tall: one connected mass of eight to ten steep cool grey stone peaks in three staggered rows, joined by saddles and shared rock faces, the highest peaks at the back with small white snow caps, big simple rock faces in two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; the massif fills the image from edge to edge; just rock and snow; the foot of the rock is the lowest thing in the image.
shared.ridgeTall: Subject: a narrow mountain range, twice as tall as it is wide, running from the top of the image to the bottom: one continuous spine of five or six steep cool grey stone peaks one behind the other, joined by saddles into a single rock mass, small white snow caps on the highest peaks, big simple rock faces in two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; just rock and snow; the foot of the rock is the lowest thing in the image.
shared.massif: Subject: a broad mountain massif: one connected mass of about nine steep cool grey stone peaks in three staggered rows, joined by saddles and shared rock faces, every peak the same size as a peak of the style image (about 28 pixels wide), the highest peaks at the back, small white snow caps on most peaks, big simple rock faces in two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; the massif is as wide as the image; just rock and snow; the foot of the rock is the lowest thing in the image.
shared.spine: Subject: a narrow mountain range running away from the viewer, from the bottom of the image to the top: one continuous spine of five steep cool grey stone peaks one behind the other, joined by saddles into a single rock mass, every peak the same size as a peak of the style image (about 28 pixels wide), small white snow caps, big simple rock faces in two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; just rock and snow; the foot of the rock is the lowest thing in the image.
shared.spineNarrow: Subject: a tall narrow mountain range in the middle of the image with empty space left and right: one continuous spine of four or five steep cool grey stone peaks stacked one behind the other from the bottom of the image to the top, joined by saddles into a single rock mass, only a third of the image wide, small white snow caps, two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; just rock and snow.
shared.massifBig: Subject: one big mountain massif nearly as tall as the image and as wide as the image: three or four large steep cool grey stone peaks with broad white snow caps that share one single rock mass, joined by high saddles and long ridgelines, big simple rock faces in two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; few large shapes, not many small peaks; just rock and snow.
shared.spineSlim: Subject: a slim mountain ridge running straight up the middle of the image from the bottom edge to the top edge, with wide empty space left and right: three large steep cool grey stone peaks one directly behind the other, sharing one rock mass, the ridge only a quarter of the image wide and almost as tall as the image, broad white snow caps, two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; just rock and snow.
shared.ridge3: Subject: a mountain ridge twice as wide as it is tall: three large steep cool grey stone peaks side by side with broad white snow caps, sharing one rock mass and joined by high saddles, each peak about a third of the image wide, low rocky foothills tapering out to the left edge and the right edge of the image, big simple rock faces in two blue-grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; few large shapes; just rock and snow.
shared.peak1: Subject: one single large steep cool grey stone mountain peak with a broad white snow cap and one small shoulder peak joined to its side, almost as wide as the image, big simple rock faces in two blue-grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; one large shape; just rock and snow.
shared.ridgeNS: Subject: a mountain ridge running away from the viewer in the middle of the image, with wide empty space left and right: two large steep cool grey stone peaks with broad white snow caps, the far peak higher up in the image and partly hidden behind the near peak, joined by one long ridgeline and shared rock faces into a single rock mass, the ridge only a third of the image wide and almost as tall as the image, two blue-grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; just rock and snow.
shared.foothill: Subject: a low rocky foothill: a small wide mound of cool grey stone with two low rounded bumps and no snow, much wider than it is tall, big simple rock faces in two blue-grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; just rock.
shared.peakSmall: Subject: one small mountain: a single steep cool grey stone peak with a white snow cap and one lower shoulder peak joined to its side, sharing one rock mass, about two thirds of the image wide, big simple rock faces in two blue-grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; whole mountain inside the image with empty space around it; just rock and snow.
shared.spineNarrow2: Subject: a tall narrow mountain range in the middle of the image with wide empty space left and right: one continuous ridge of four steep cool grey stone peaks one behind the other running straight from the bottom of the image to the top, joined by saddles into a single rock mass, only a quarter of the image wide, small white snow caps, two grey tones, the same rock, outline and palette as the style image; just rock and snow.

recipes.subject: @ridgeWide
recipes.notes: Sample: the style-image route that gave the best forest pieces in the research.
recipes.review: 0 and 2: clean ridges of joined snow-capped peaks, used (2x1 d, and in the 2x2 massifs). 1: a diagonal massif, unused. 3: a cluster of separate rounded peaks, unused.

recipes.subject: @ridgeSquare
recipes.reject: Huge flat triangles with no snow, cut off at the top: style and scale drift (one candidate above 170 px).

recipes.subject: @ridgeWide
recipes.notes: Sample: the batch pipeline's own endpoint at the piece canvas, for comparison.
recipes.reject: Peaks and trees on an isometric grass slab, as Pixen draws tall terrain at a large canvas.

recipes.subject: @massif
recipes.notes: A 2x2 massif at 160 x 168: sides up to 170 px return four candidates.
recipes.review: Four massifs of about ten small peaks each. On the board they read as a crowd of little rocks, not a range, so none is used (s08 replaced them).

recipes.subject: @spine
recipes.reject: Four small clusters, none of them a range two cells tall, and each cut off at the left or right image edge.

recipes.subject: @ridgeWide
recipes.review: Unused. 2 was a 2x1 variant in the first set, but it is brown-grey and darker than the blue-grey set; 0, 1 and 3 are broken or without snow.

recipes.subject: @spineNarrow
recipes.notes: A 1x2 spine asked for on a wide canvas with empty sides, so nothing is cut at 80 px; only candidates at most 80 px wide can be used.
recipes.review: 0: a ridge of five peaks running away from the viewer, 77 px wide, used for both 1x2 pieces (the second mirrored). 1 to 3: 94 or 95 px wide, too wide for one column, unused.

recipes.subject: @massifBig
recipes.notes: A 2x2 massif of a few large peaks: the first massifs were a crowd of small peaks on the board.
recipes.review: Massifs of three or four peaks about 65 px wide and 110 px tall. They were the 2x2 pieces of the first set, but next to the ridges they read as mountains of twice the scale. Unused; s08-0 served as a style image for s10 to s13.

recipes.subject: @spineSlim
recipes.review: Three cones stacked one above the other: not a ridge. Unused.

recipes.subject: @ridge3
recipes.notes: 2x1 ridges at the peak scale of the s08 massifs, styled from one of them.
recipes.review: Four near-copies of the style image (an s08 massif) at 156 x 104: too tall for a one-row ridge. A style image that fills its canvas is copied, not followed. Unused.

recipes.subject: @peak1
recipes.notes: Single peaks in the range style and scale.
recipes.reject: Crops of the style massif, cut at every image edge.

recipes.subject: @ridgeNS
recipes.reject: Copies of the style massif, 156 px wide: not a one-column ridge.

recipes.subject: @foothill
recipes.notes: A low join piece drawn between two ranges.
recipes.review: Sixteen low grey rocks, tried as join pieces between two ridges (9 and 1, after 2 and 10 were too dark). On the board they read as grey slugs lying between the ridges, so the joins were dropped. Unused.

recipes.subject: @peakSmall
recipes.notes: Single mountains in the scale of the s01 ridges.
recipes.review: Sixteen single mountains at the ridge scale. 4 (a jagged peak with foothills) and 7 (a peak with two shoulders) are used as the 1x1 pieces; most others are the old cluster of four rounded peaks again.

recipes.subject: @ridgeWide
recipes.notes: More ridges by the s01 recipe, another seed.
recipes.review: Four clean blue-grey ridges of five peaks, all used (2x1 a, b, c and in the 2x2 massifs).

recipes.subject: @spineNarrow2
recipes.review: Four ridges lying across the image, 115 px wide: not a one-column ridge. Unused.

pieces.notes: Single mountains generated at the scale of the ridges.
A ridge running north to south.
A massif: two ridges of the same scale one behind the other, the front one overlapping the foot of the back one.
